Footnote: The provision 3.43 (iii) will no longer exist once the post of Additional Director is abolished altogether in all the services of the Lok Sabha Secretariat. 23 CHAPTER IV SECURITY OF OFFICIAL INFORMATION AND DOCUMENTS 4.1 Rule 14 of the Lok Sabha Secretariat (Conduct) Rules, 1955 (as amended) provides as follows: “No officer/official shall, unless generally or specially permitted by the Secretary-General, or in the performance in good faith of the duties assigned to him/her, communicate directly or indirectly any official documents/papers or any part thereof or information which has come into his/her possession in the course of his/her official duties, or has been prepared or collected by him/her in the course of those duties, whether from official source or otherwise, to any other officer of the Secretariat or to other Government Servant or to any private person or to the Press to whom he/she is not authorised to communicate such document or information.” As per this Rule, officers/officials of the Secretariat are prohibited from communicating to any one (without good authority) any information acquired by them in the course of their official duties. It shall be the duty of all the employees to steadfastly see that, discrete official information is not disclosed to anyone who is not connected officially with such matters, even through conduct in which there is no deliberately harmful intent, such as idle gossip, the desire to appear important by being ‘in the know’, the furtherance of collective or family interests, or the desire to gratify a person towards whom an obligation is felt. Particular care should be used in conversation with or in the hearing of persons who may have a motive for obtaining some particular piece of information or Press Correspondents whose business is to get and publish news. Definition of Secret/Confidential Documents/Papers. (i) Secret/Confidential information is any information with restrictions placed on its dissemination. The Secretariat often holds and manages large amounts of confidential information. Improper use of this information can constitute corrupt conduct. (ii) Common corruption risks associated with Secret/confidential information include: a. public official providing confidential information to a third party to assist that party to gain an advantage, for example, during a tendering process; b. public official using personal information about a client for private purposes, such as debt collection, fraud, stalking or other harassment, or providing such information to others for these purposes; c. public official enabling others to improperly access confidential information; d. former public official providing confidential information to their new private sector employer to assist the employer to gain an advantage. (iii) Lists of key drivers that could lead to employees missing confidential information, includes: a. Curiosity. b. To obtain a material benefit. c. To benefit friends, family members and associates. Classification of Confidential Papers 4.2 In the Secretariat, the following shall be the classification of Confidential Papers: Official 4.3 This is the majority of information that is created or processed by the Secretariat, which may include routine official operations and services, some of which could have damaging consequences if lost, stolen, or published in the media, but which are not subject to sensitive threat outline. This classification applies to the vast majority of Government information (including general administration, public safety, criminal justice, and law enforcement etc.), and need to be taken care. 24 Official-Sensitive 4.4 Limited information of the majority of information that is created / processed by the Secretariat remains Officially Sensitive for being shared outside of routine or well understood official process. These few activities related information or cases require the official-sensitive marking, along with information previously marked as confidential. Also, from amongst information normally marked as protected or restricted, individual cases/ instances which are sensitive (marked confidential on an individual basis) may be identified by adding ‘sensitive’, and must therefore be marked ‘official-sensitive’. This marking alerts users to the enhanced level of risk and that additional controls are required in their dissemination. Confidential 4.5 This marking is reserved for papers containing information, the unauthorised disclosure of which while not endangering the national security would be prejudicial to the interest of the Nation, any Government activity or individual or would cause administrative embarrassment or difficulty or be of the advantage to a foreign nation. Personal—Not for Publication 4.6 This marking is reserved for communication to the members of the Public when it is desired to make it clear that these communications or the information contained therein should not be published. Secret 4.7 Very sensitive information that justifies heightened protective measures to defend against determined or highly capability threats, whereby, compromise might seriously damage military capabilities, international relations or the investigation of serious organised crime etc. or unauthorised disclosure of such documents/ papers containing information would endanger National security, cause serious injury to the interest or prestige of the Nation or serious embarrassment to Government or would be of great advantage to a foreign Nation, are marked Secret. Top Secret 4.8 Most sensitive information, requiring the highest levels of protection from the most serious threats, where compromise might cause widespread loss of life or else threaten the security or economic wellbeing of the Country or friendly Nations. This classification remains for information of the highest sensitivity relating to National Security and subject to highly capable threat sources. Any official business area holding or expecting to hold information at this level, such as Parliament Security Service, shall be kept with the Secretary General for controls. Top Secret marking must be reserved for documents/papers containing information on National Security, which must not be disclosed to any one for whom it is not essential to have knowledge of it for the proper performance of his/her duty. Such documents/papers include references to current or future Military operations, intending movements or dispositions of armed forces, shaping of secret methods of war, matters of high international and internal political policy, cyphers and reports derived from secret sources of intelligence. The distribution of documents/papers having ‘Top Secret’ classification must be limited to the minimum number of persons concerned, and in such cases, it will not be safer to err on issues of security. Applying the Classification System 4.9 The following considerations must be taken into account: a. All Officers/Officials of the Secretariat are responsible for ensuring the safe keeping of all confidential/sensitive information with care, to enable the official business/function in smooth manner. b. The majority of information created and or received from wider Governmental department/ institutions falls into the Official tier; information of Secret and Top Secret nature, essential for national security and the very highest threat areas, needs a procedure higher than all Official/ Normal Information. 25 c. Official Information provides for a general/sufficient level of control of information (including for systems holding such information) which is not subject to heightened threat sources. However, within this, there is flexibility to apply additional operational controls to reflect sensitivity of select information. d. Most areas of activity in the Secretariat at the level of Official information, Staff follows existing instructions and procedures for handling information that apply to those activities. However, such instructions should include provisions for identifying and dealing with more Sensitive information. e. Instructions of an appropriate authority in the hierarchy must be taken into account by Officers/ Officials who agree to receive, handle, take control or otherwise process any information of Secret or Top Secret in a strict manner. Procedure for managing Secret/Confidential papers/documents 4.10 The following procedure will be observed with regard to the treatment and safeguarding of secret and confidential information and papers: a. The Branch Officer will invariably determine whether a particular paper/document received are to be classified as ‘Secret’ or ‘Confidential’ information. b. Documents/Papers which may be ‘Secret or Confidential’ until the occurrence of some particular event or announcement will not be treated as such, afterwards the occurrence of the Event. c. All Secret and Confidential documents/papers must be typed in the presence of the Officer who has dictated or initiated the same. Such a file, in any case, must be retained in the personal custody of such Officer, with only such papers required by the stenographer/typist as are essential for the typing work in hand must be parted. All drafts, rough notes and other routine papers will invariably be destroyed as soon as the fair copy of the letter, note, etc., has been issued. The pages of stenographer’s notebook, in which dictation of Secret/Confidential papers has been taken, should be destroyed or kept in safe custody for destruction by the concerned Officer. d. All Secret/Confidential information/material for photocopying through the ‘D’ Branch, in the presence of such an Officer, the needful must be done without any delay, and the copies made and the original material must be returned to the Officer on the spot. Unauthorised/extra copies of such documents/papers must be strictly avoided. (Appendix X) e. The Officers/Branches dealing with Secret documents/papers will maintain a register for recording the number of copies of such papers received after photocopying from the Distribution Branch and their utilization (Appendix XI). f. Documents/Papers marked Secret/Confidential must not be sent through ordinary course by the Office, but must be distinguished and dealt with only by Officers/Officials explicitly authorised in that behalf. If not passed by hand from one authorised person to another, they will be sent in sealed covers or in the boxes provided for this purpose, which are fitted with special locks. The possession of keys for these boxes will be permitted only to persons particularly authorised and the safe custody of the keys will be a matter of great importance for which each authorised Officer will be personally responsible. g. Papers marked Secret/Confidential must be dealt by the Head of the Branch or by a thoroughly reliable dealing hand. They will be registered or given a file No. by the concerned Official without disclosing the subject. h. All covers marked Secret/Confidential, if not addressed to an Officer by name, will be sent to the Branch Officer by the Receipt Assistant in ‘D’ Branch. i. None of the Secret or Confidential documents/papers must be left lying in the Officers’ Room or in the Branches where unauthorised persons might obtain access to them. Such documents/papers must be kept locked in secure manner. j. Fair copies of Secret/Confidential material containing secret or confidential information must be kept in the personal custody of the reliable officials particularly authorised for the safe custody of 26 secret or confidential papers. Files in the computer containing secret or confidential information must be encoded with appropriate password known only to the reliable officials. k. When sent by post, Secret/Confidential documents/papers must be enclosed in double covers of which the inner one will be pasted or sealed and marked ‘Confidential’ or ‘Secret’ and superscripted with the name of the Officer by whom it is to be opened. The outer cover will bear the usual official address. Letters or packets containing Secret/Confidential documents/papers sent by post must invariably be ‘Registered’ and be sent with “acknowledgement due”. l. Secret/Confidential files, when recorded must be kept under the supervision of the Head of the Branch concerned for their safe custody. Every classified file (other than confidential) must be reviewed once in five years for declassification. A declassified file considered fit for permanent preservation must be transferred to the Parliamentary Museum and Archives. m. For documents/papers of ‘Top Secret’ and ‘Secret’ nature to be transmitted by hand must be provided/delivered in a single cover, carefully sealed and marked with the correct name, address and security marking, before being entrusted to the hand of a reliable dealing hand who will be handing/delivering directly to the Officer addressed. n. Instructions for Officers/Officials (i) Regarding ‘Custody of Papers’, Rule 383 of the Rules of Procedure and Conduct of Business in Lok Sabha provides that “The Secretary-General shall have custody of all records, documents and papers belonging to the House or any of its Committees or Lok Sabha Secretariat and he/she shall not permit any such records, documents or papers to be taken from the Parliament House without the permission of the Speaker”. This rule should be brought to the knowledge of all the Officers/Officials for strict compliance. (ii) In case a verbal or written communication is received from the Ministries or Departments or from anyone not connected with this Secretariat for the supply of any information directly or indirectly related to Parliament or Lok Sabha Secretariat, it should not be communicated to anyone outside the Lok Sabha Secretariat without the express orders of Secretary-General. (iii) While dealing with verbal enquiry or written request made by or received from any person of a Ministry/Department or by other organizations eliciting information on any matter which may be in the custody of any official of the Secretariat, such a person may be requested to contact the Branch Officer concerned instead. Under no circumstances must such information be divulged by any officer or staff of this Secretariat unless he/she are satisfied that the supply of such information is definitely allowed under general or specific orders by the Secretary-General on the subject. (iv) In the event of a request being received in writing and the information is required immediately; it should be submitted quickly by the Branch dealing with the matter through proper channel for the orders of the Secretary-General. Till such time as the Secretary-General has passed orders on the file, no information need be furnished even though the person seeking the information is pressing for it. (v) In cases where information is asked for by a person (whether an official of a Ministry/Department or an outsider) after normal working hours when it may be difficult to contact the Branch Officer or any higher authority, the person seeking the information may be politely asked to renew his/her request on the following day, when it may be possible to obtain the orders of the Branch Officer concerned. (vi) In rare cases when information is immediately required beyond working hours, the Head of the Branch dealing with the matter should try to contact the Branch Officer at his/her residence over the telephone/mobile and if per chance the Branch Officer be not available, he/she should ring up Divisional Officer (Director or Officer holding equivalent rank)/Joint Secretary/ Additional Secretary/Secretary/Secretary-General at residence and obtain orders. 27 (vii) In cases where the Branch Officer himself/herself has any doubt as to whether the information asked for should or should not be furnished, he/she should immediately take the orders of the higher officer(s). (viii) Every official of this Secretariat should make it a point that no person who is not an employee of the Lok Sabha Secretariat is allowed to see the files or papers without the permission of the Branch Officer or if in doubt without the express orders of Divisional Officer (Director or Officer holding equivalent rank)/Joint Secretary/Additional Secretary/Secretary/Secretary- General. (ix) No unauthorised outsider should be allowed to watch the working of the officials/staff etc., in the office rooms, and any official business with outsiders should be concluded quickly and they should be politely asked to leave the room after such business is concluded. o. Joint Secretary(S) has been put in general charge of all the security arrangements in the Parliament House Complex and will act as a Liaison Officer in matters concerning the treatment and safeguarding of secret and confidential information and papers, between the Lok Sabha Secretariat and different security agencies like Intelligence Bureau, SPG, NSG and Delhi Police, etc. Procedure for Secret/Confidential Communications from Ministries for Parliamentary Questions 4.11 The following procedure will be observed for dealing with Secret/Confidential Communications received from the Ministries regarding questions: (a) Secret/Confidential Communications will be received by the officers concerned in whose name these have been marked. (b) The officer concerned will deal with such cases himself/herself. Relevant file may be called for from the Branch. (c) In case the file is to be referred to other officers for obtaining his/her opinion, it will be marked Confidential/Secret in red ink in bold letters and put in a special folder meant for this purpose. Such files will be transmitted from one officer to another through their PAs. The Officers concerned will ensure that the file is received back within a reasonable time. (d) After final orders on the admissibility or otherwise of a question have been passed, the officer concerned will remove the Secret/Confidential Communication from the file and indicate the fact therein. The relevant extract of the decision will be placed on the file for further action and the file will be returned to the Branch after deleting the Secret/Confidential marking. (e) Such Secret/Confidential Communications will be kept in the custody of the officer concerned. (f) It is expected of the Officers/PAs who handle the Secret/Confidential Communications that their contents remain sacrosanct and are not divulged to any unauthorised personnel. Secret/Confidential documents/papers must not be transmitted through F AX/e-mail or insecure Computer Terminal/Laptop/any other electronic mode 4.12 While handling secret/confidential documents/papers needing official protection, instructions for safeguarding of such documents/papers issued by the Lok Sabha Secretariat from time to time should be strictly adhered to by all the Officers/Officials of the Secretariat. Classified topics must not be discussed on unencrypted phone lines, classified information should not be processed on insecure computers, and classified documents have to be stored in locked safes. Records management of protected information and assets 4.13 The Secretariat must maintain records of protected and classified information and assets by establishing adequate record office facilities for receiving, distributing and storing such information and assets. 28 Instructions for recording of classified information and assets (i) Any classified information and assets must be recorded indicating the dates, names and transactions details such as: a. receipt by the Record Office b. distribution within the Secretariat c. creation within the Secretariat d. reproduction within the Secretariat e. destruction within the Secretariat f. transmittal outside the Secretariat (ii) Transmittal of such information and assets outside the Secretariat must be performed as per instructions issued from time to time by the Administration. Written records of distribution, circulation and return within the Secretariat must include receipt by signature, of the Officers/Officials involved. Officers/ Officials who have access to classified information and assets must be briefed on their responsibilities for its protection, and any special restrictions concerning its use or further dissemination by the head of such Unit. (iii) All records of classified information and assets must be made available for the annual inspection by the specific Joint Secretary of the Branch/Unit, and must be approved by the Secretary General. Instructions for Security of Records Room/Branch and classified information 4.14 Management of records office, where protected and classified information is stored or processed must ensure the following procedures: a. As a minimum, this Room/Branch must be managed as a security zone. b. Records Room/Branch Official/staff who have access to protected and classified information must hold a reliability status or personnel security clearance to the highest level required. c. Protected and classified information must be filed and circulated in marked file jackets that clearly indicate that they contain protected and classified information. d. A protected file must be marked according to the highest level of sensitivity retained in the file. e. Areas where mail is opened must be managed according to ‘D’ Branch mailroom security standards. f. Release/dissemination of confidential/protected files from this Records Room/Branch must be limited to employees with reliability status with a need-to-know. g. Release of ‘Top Secret’ and ‘Secret’ files from this Records Room/Branch must be limited to appropriately security-cleared employees with a need-to-know. Such Officer/Official who has been authorised access to deal must be identified on an access list approved by Secretary General or an appropriate competent authority. h. Classified information of foreign origin must be accorded the same protection as information of equivalent classification of India possessed by the Secretariat. Precautions during use 4.15 Special care must be taken to safeguard against disclosure or unauthorized access when protected and classified information and assets are removed from approved storage containers. Specific points to observe are: a. Do not leave protected and classified information and assets unattended. b. Ensure that protected and classified information and assets cannot be viewed, or discussion of it overheard, by persons not possessing reliability screening or the appropriate level of clearance or without a need-to-know. 29 CHAPTER V MANAGEMENT OF FILES AND RECORDS 5.1 Record management pertains to numerous activities pertaining to creation and use of records, classification, retention and processes related to review and weeding out of records. Decision making and disposal of cases in files several times require consultation of old records and knowledge of precedents. Thus record management is extremely crucial for location of references, to ensure continuity in decision making, to provide the requisite evidence in case of disputes and to preserve records of historical and research value. Recording of Files and Papers 5.2 After action on all the issues under consideration has been completed, files need to be closed and recorded as per the laid down procedures. The laid down procedures may be issued in the form of Routine Orders by the Branch/Branches indicating various subjects of the files being dealt in the Branch, their Class/ Category and their retention period with the approval of JS concerned and the same may be incorporated in the Branch Procedure & Practice V olume(s) as a separate chapter for permanent record. Thus, when no further action is required to be taken on a file, the Dealing Hand will put up to the Head of the Branch for orders/approval in the Note portion of the File for the file being closed and recorded.The Head of the Branch will ensure that all orders in the file have been complied with, all part files are merged into the main file and no further action/correspondence is pending. Thereafter, she/he will submit it to the Branch officer (Deputy Secretary or an officer of equivalent rank) for approval. 5.3 Files will be recorded under any one of the following classes broadly:— (a) Class ‘A’ meaning ‘keep and print or digitise’—This classification will be adopted for: (i) files of historical importance such as papers relating to the origin of Secretariat, Committees and their functions; (ii) files relating to major policy decisions and the implementation of a change of policy including a complete set of instructions there under; (iii) files containing direct reference to trends or developments in political, social, economic or other fields, and important aspects of scientific or technical research and development; (iv) files providing lasting precedents for important procedure, e.g. administrative memoranda, historical reports and summaries and legal opinion on important matters; (v) files containing rules, regulations, departmental instructions or guidelines of general application; (vi) files relating to important litigation or ‘causes celebres’ in which the administration was involved; (vii) important rulings/decisions of the Hon’ble Speaker or the Secretary-General and decisions relating to the service conditions of the staff which are not embodied in any Rules, etc. (viii) files containing papers which are important or are likely to become important in future, however, indirectly as source of information on any aspect of history, whether political, military, social, economic etc. or which are, or may in future prove to be of biographical or antiquarian interest; and (ix) material likely to be required frequently for reference in future. (b) Class ‘B’ meaning ‘keep but do not Print or Digitise’—This class will also cover files which contain orders and instructions, etc., of permanent importance but which are not likely to be required very frequently for reference. 30 (c) Class ‘C’ meaning ‘Keep for specified period only’—This class will consist of files of secondary importance which are to be preserved for limited periods of 3, 5 or 10 years. 5.4 No file will be included in class ‘A’ without the approval of the Additional Secretary/Joint Secretary. As the subjects of the files would be different in every Branch, therefore, it is difficult to provide an exhaustive list covering all the subjects of various Branches/Units of Lok Sabha Secretariat. Destruction of Ephemeral Files 5.5 Papers which are of a purely ephemeral nature, such as manuscripts, proofs, etc. of printed publications, will not be recorded but shall be filed and kept separately for one year, after which these papers would be destroyed. Preparing a File for Record 5.6 After a file has been marked for record, it should be arranged properly for recording. This would involve the following action:— (a) Amendment or revision of the title of the file, where necessitated by the development of the subject matters of the case since its start. (b) Completion of references, that is removing alphabetical slips/flags and giving permanent identification marks to the references quoted in notes and correspondence (where this has not already been done) and marking numbers of previous or later files on the subject on the cover of the file. (c) Preparation, where necessary, of a fresh cover for the file with the revised title and details of previous and later references, etc., neatly typed. (d) Removal of routine notes and papers from the files which are to be weeded out. (e) Noting in the file register the classification and date of recording. (f) Giving indication about the life of the file on the cover. (g) Obtaining orders of the Branch Officer whether the file is to be summarised or not for the purpose of incorporation of important decision in the Precedents Register, if not already done so and writing on the cover ‘Recorded and Summarised’ or ‘Not summarised’ as the case may be. (h) Files recorded under class ‘A’ will be edited for printing by the dealing hand in accordance with the instructions given in this Chapter. 5.7 In all printed or bound files a coloured sheet or ‘separator’ should be included between the correspondence and the notes. Papers which are not of sufficient importance to form part of the main file, but have relation to the subject matter of the file, will be retained as ‘KW papers’ by inserting a sheet after the correspondences. 5.8 The file will, thereafter, be handed over to the Branch Attendant/Messenger, who after stitching neatly, will hand it over to the Branch SA/SSA/AEO. Recorded files will be kept serially in the Branch/Unit concerned for not more than 3 years. Thereafter, they will be transferred to the Record Room of the Records Branch. 5.9 When the file is stitched, the same will be submitted to Head of Branch for signature. Custody of files 5.10 With a view to having a permanent record about the ultimate disposal of a file, all files will be sent to the Record Room by the SA/SSA of the Branch concerned, who will make an entry in the relevant column of the File Register against the file concerned. 5.11 While sending files to main Record Room, two lists will be prepared by Branches, in the form shown in Appendix XII & XIII. One copy will be retained by the Record Room and other returned to the Branch concerned. 31 5.12 The Records Branch will maintain Record Review Register in which a few pages will be allotted for each future year. Files marked for review in a particular year will be entered in the pages earmarked for that year in the register. 5.13 When printed copies of files have been received and compared with the original, one copy will be kept in the Branch concerned and the original file along with the remaining printed copies will be sent to the Record Room. 5.14 Recorded files which are marked secret/confidential should be retained by the Head of the Branch concerned for safe custody . 5.15 The weeding out of the files after their retention period is over may be done as per the proforma enclosed as Appendix XIA. If the Branch concerned desires to have a different proforma for weeding out files, the Branch may accordingly modify the proforma as per its requirements. 5.16 The Lok Sabha Secretariat will maintain a Records Branch who will be responsible for maintenance of records room for stocking or safe keeping of copy of Bills, debates, Report of Parliamentary Committees, Parliamentary and Branch Publications, Files, etc. received from Branches/Units of the Secretariat. The Erstwhile Sales and Records Branch of the Secretariat was reorganized into two separate entities – (i) Records Branch (ii) Sales Unit under General Stores Branch vide Office Order Part I No.2219, dated 23.06.2020. The Records Branch is responsible for maintenance of records of Branches, retrieval/review of old files/records, weeding out debates, Bills, etc. and retrieval of files and other Parliamentary publications for use and reference of various Branches. 5.17 Classification of Records The record of the Secretariat is classified into three categories, viz.: — Category I Bills, Report of Select/Joint Committees on Bills, Opinion on Bills, Periodicals, Debates, etc. Category II Report of Parliamentary Committees. Category III Recorded files and Register. 5.18 I. Copy of only those Bills, Reports, Files, Periodicals, Debates, Registers, etc. which are required to be preserved permanently shall be sent from Branches/ Units in the prescribed format signed by Head of the Branch to the Records Branch (Appendix XIV). Copy of Bills, Reports, Files, Publications, Periodicals, etc. which are required for day to day use of the Branches/Units, shall be kept by themselves either in their rooms or in their own Record Rooms. After the copy/copies of the Bills/Reports/Publications, etc. have been received and accepted in the Records, the entries regarding title of the publication, number of copies received, etc. are made in the Stock Register(s) maintained for the purpose. The copies shall thereafter be placed in the rack/ compactor earmarked for each Branch at the relevant places. The Important Periodicals or those having archival/historical value may be retained till the process of digitization is complete. Files of category C (to be preserved upto 10 years) will be accepted by Records Branch only if there is availability of space in the Branch. II. Procedure for consigning of Files to Record Room The Consigning Branch/Unit should ensure the following: i. Before sending files to the Record Room, they should be sorted out and arranged year and number- wise by the consigning Branch/Unit. Files of the same year should be arranged and entered in the list serially and according to the ascending order of their file numbers. ii. Old files and new files should be entered in separate lists, in duplicate. Old files are those which were once requisitioned from the Record Room for reference purpose and new files are those which are being consigned to the Record Room for the first time. 32 iii. Files should be sent to the Record Room only after they have been finally closed and ordered to be recorded. iv. Similar files opened on the same subject in the same year through an over-sight or for dealing urgent papers in the event of main file being under action/submission should be amalgamated into one file before consigning to the Record Room. v. No loose papers etc. will be sent to the Record Room until they are made into files and given a regular file number. Part files will not be sent for consigning. vi. The following papers should be removed from files being prepared for consignment: (a) Unnecessary covers. (b) Reminders and explanations for delay if the required answer has been received or sent, if they do not bear serial numbers. (c) Rough copies of initialed faired drafts. (d) Proofs of finally printed papers. (e) Office Slips. vii. Where the Note portion is separate, it should be stitched at the end of the correspondence portion of the file. The order for recording the file should be the last proceeding on the Note portion. The Head of the Branch will sign the order for recording the file. viii. Files that are to be retained permanently should not be mixed up with other files in the same list nor should the files that are returned from the Record Room for correction be sent back to the Record Room or entered in the same list under which new files are being consigned. Such files should be returned to the Record Room within a week after necessary corrections, through the list under which they were sent by the Record Room. ix. Before files are consigned to the Record Room, the threads binding the file should be given a double knot and the remaining portions of both the ends of the threads should be clipped so that the recorded files cannot be re-opened. The files along with the challan list in duplicate (one copy to be returned by Record Room) are then sent to the Record Room. If the files are not received in accordance with the above procedure, the in-charge of the Record Room should not accept them. Issue and Return of Publications/Files 5.19 Copy of publication/File shall be supplied to the Branches by the Records Branch only against requisition slips in prescribed form signed by the Head of the Branch concerned as given in Appendix XV . In case the requisition is required by the Branch other than the Branch to which the publication relates, the requisition shall be routed through the Head of the Branch concerned. 5.20 All files requisitioned from the Records Branch shall be returned by the Branch concerned within a period of two months from the date of issue, unless otherwise requested. If the file is required for a longer period by the Branch, the Branch concerned shall arrange to send a fresh requisition slip after the expiry of one month. The requisition register should be reviewed each week and reminders sent in respect of overdue files. The old files requisitioned and returned to the Record Room in which no alteration in the period of retention is made should be restored to their proper places after these have been thoroughly checked to ensure that they are intact. The Branches/Units requisitioning old files from the Record Room shall follow the following instructions:– (i) Branches/Units should return the files obtained on requisition to the Record Room immediately after purpose is served, and obtain the signatures of the record clerk on the copy of the forwarding note. (ii) Recorded files, requisitioned from the Record Room for reference purpose, should never be reopened to deal with fresh receipts. 33 Retrieval of Records The utility of records to an organisation depends upon as to how best and how quickly the information could be retrieved from them. For efficient retrieval of information an ‘Index’ to records is prepared wherein index slips are made in the first instance under the subject i.e. standards heads which may serve as catch-word or by name, place, etc. giving cross-references. Thereafter, these index slips have to be arranged alphabetically. The process can also be computerised. The Index sometimes called a schedule, abstract or docket is usually a tabulated statement arranged in chronological order of the documents, briefly showing the important features of each document and mentioning the names of the parties between whom the correspondence has passed. Preservation of Records 5.21 Longevity of records depends upon the storage environment. It shall be the responsibility of the Records Branch to ensure that the publications, files, etc. which are sent to them by the Branches are neat and clean, are preserved in the best possible condition and that those are not damaged in any way. The bundles of files, etc. shall be kept in a methodical and systematic manner in the racks. 5.22 Proper storage will require removal of dust, fumigation, anti-rodent action, etc. Proper records should be stored on wooden/steel racks, and should never be kept on the floor. The Record Room should be free from seepage of water from the floor, walls and ceiling. It shall be ensured that dusting, fumigation, etc. is done regularly and that naphthalene bricks are kept invariably for preservation of publications and files. Suitable fire-fighting equipment should be installed and record room staff given periodic training. 5.23 Recommended Practices to ensure Longevity of Records — The following points may be observed:– (i) Good quality paper and ink should be used, especially in files likely to be of value. (ii) Documents should be kept flat and not in folded shape. (iii) Documents should not be kept loose and use of metal pins and clips should be avoided while keeping it. (iv) Steel racks or steel almirahs are preferable to wooden ones for storage of files. (v) Indirect diffused lighting is preferable in a record room. (vi) Atmospheric pollution, excessive heat, humidity and dryness are harmful to records. (vii) Naphthalene bricks or balls (wrapped in tissue paper) should be used to act as an insect repellent; the use of insecticidal sprays directly on the records is to be avoided. (viii) Smoking and eating in the stack area should not be allowed. (ix) Carbon dioxide type fire extinguishers should be provided in the Record Room. (x) Repairs of brittle and damaged manuscript or books should be undertaken under the guidance of experts. (xi) Periodic fumigation and use of vacuum cleaner machine. Review and Weeding Out of Records 5.24 In order to ascertain how much of the records that have been stored have lost their relevance or utility, it is essential that records be systematically and regularly reviewed. Ephemeral records will be weeded out without any further review, while other records will be required to be reviewed before being weeded out. Records already classified, will be reviewed after the expiry of the specified retention period and will be:– (i) either weeded out; or (ii) retained for a further specified period from the year of closing, at the end of which it will be weeded out without any further review; or 34 (iii) upgraded to higher class with the approval of the Branch Officer of the consigning Branch for reasons to be stated; (iv) Class ‘A’ and Class ‘B’ files will be reviewed on attaining the 25 th year of their life. In these reviews, the need for revising the original classification of class ‘B’ files may be considered i.e. Upgradation to class ‘A’ or degradation to class ‘C’; (v) The year of review of class ‘C’ files be recorded with reference to the year of their closing and that for class ‘A’ and class ‘B’ files with reference to the year of their opening. 5.25 All Branches are required to review their files/registers/Reports/documents, etc. on annual basis, unless otherwise requested to undertake review at short intervals, with a view to determine their retention or otherwise. Beginning in January each year, SA/SSA in Records Branch; or the SA/SSA of Branch records room will send to the Branches concerned the files which became due for review in the preceding year together with a list of files. 5.26 Files received for review in the concerned Branches will be examined, by respective dealing hands. Those files that are no longer required will be marked for destruction, with the approval of Head of the Branch. Other files may be marked for further retention as prescribed. For convenient retrieval, the covers of files may be stamped with the letters ‘R’ or ‘D’, to indicate whether the file should be retained or destroyed. For files which are marked for weeding out, an entry to this effect will be made in the file register against the file classification number, duly attested by Head of the Branch. 5.27 While reviewing and weeding out files, great care should be taken by the concerned Branch to ensure that the following types of cases are not destroyed:– (i) Important decisions of the Speaker or the Secretary General. (ii) Decisions relating to service conditions of the staff which are not embodied in any Rules etc. (iii) Precedents relating to the position of the Secretariat vis-a-vis the Executive/Government. (iv) Important decisions on requests for any information or any other concessions. (v) Files containing papers which are important or are likely to become important in future, as source of information on any aspect of history, whether political, military, social, economic, etc., or which are, or may in future prove to be of biographical or antiquarian interest. 5.28 While reviewing the recorded files for weeding out purposes, the following instructions should be observed:– (i) References to earlier and later files should be indicated on the covers of the relevant files, if they are not already there. (ii) If the covers of files, which are to be retained, are found to be spoiled or torn they should be replaced by new ones and torn pages should be carefully pasted. (iii) Each category should be listed and the lists submitted to the Branch Officer with recommendations for preserving or weeding out, as the case may be. (iv) Thereafter, indication whether the file should be ‘retained’ or ‘destroyed’ should be given on the Cover of the file and initiated by the Head of the Branch. (v) After marking in the file Register about the disposal regarding files to be destroyed, the remaining files which are to be retained should be returned to the Record Room. (vi) At the time of review of files for weeding out on the expiry of the specified retention period, appropriate care should be taken to ensure that important information (in the form of an OM or a letter or in any other form) as is likely to be used in future in the light of section 8(3) of the Right to Information Act, 2005 may be retained even after destruction of the file/ record, unless such information has already been published or put on the website of Lok Sabha. The concerned Branch Officer(s) should apply their wisdom while taking decision in this regard. 35 Bills, Opinions on Bills and Extracts of Debates relating to Bills 5.29 These consist ordinarily of Bills at their various stages and papers connected with that, i.e. Bills as introduced, Opinions and Precise of Opinions on Bills, Extracts from Debates relating to Bills which were circulated, Select Committee Reports, Bills as passed by Parliament, etc. In order to decide which of these should be retained and which to be weeded out, the Legislative Branches I and II should examine their stock position and importance and prepare a comprehensive statement in two lists—one enumerating the documents which are considered of importance for the present or for future purposes, and the other those which are to be weeded out. The first list should also show how many copies of each are to be retained, excess being weeded out. The number of copies of various documents to be retained in the record room will ordinarily be as shown in Appendix XVI. 5.30 The two lists with the recommendations thereon as indicated in the preceding paragraph should then be submitted to the Branch Officer for orders. 5.31 On receipt of the orders, two copies of the lists will be sent to the Record SA/SSA with clear instructions for the disposal of the documents. The Record SA/SSA should return the duplicate copy of the statement to the Legislative Branch-I or II, as the case may be after initialing it in token of having received the statement. He/ she will also make necessary entries in the appropriate registers. 5.32 The Legislative Branches-I and II should also maintain a complete set of important documents which may be required for reference, properly bound, with all connected documents in their correct sequence. Manuscripts and corrected proofs of Debates 5.33 The manuscripts and corrected proofs of Parliamentary Debates, Hindi and English versions both, will be weeded out after the printed Debates are received from printers and released for distribution. The original papers relating to original version of Debate such as corrections from Ministers/Members in their speeches, Division Lists and other papers from Table Office, communications from Legislative Branches I & II, Question Branch, Reporters Branch, LT Nos. from Parliament Library, corrected Question Lists and other essential papers will be preserved by the Editorial Branch till the English and Hindi Versions of Debates are printed and their release order issued. The concerned Branches shall send a copy of the release order to Editorial Branch. Thereafter, these papers would be weeded out under the orders of Branch Officer. Shorthand notebooks of proceedings 5.34 The Reporters will preserve their shorthand notebooks for a period of three months from the last date to which the proceedings in the notebook relate and after the said-period, they may be destroyed. Books, Reports, Debates, Newspapers, Journals & Periodicals in the Library 5.35 Books, reports, pamphlets and other publications which have ceased to be of any further use will be weeded out from time to time in the Library. Proposals for weeding out shall be submitted through the Branch Officers indicating the reasons for the action proposed and denote the number of copies to be retained or weeded out and the orders of the concerned Director/Joint Secretary should be sought therein. 5.36 The following general principles shall be followed in recommending the weeding of books etc. in the Library:— (a) Law books will be weeded out after the newer editions of the same have been received. (b) Only those Reports will be weeded out which are of a very temporary nature and not worth preserving as old records. (c) Only those books and publications etc. will be weeded out which are not considered worth preserving in a library of Parliament. (d) Debates/Acts of Parliament and other legislative bodies will not be weeded out. 36 5.37 The following guidelines will be observed regarding number of copies to be retained in respect of various The proposals will clearly indicate the reasons for the action proposed and denote the number of copies to be retained or weeded out. 5.40 Before weeding out the copies of the Debates, publications or reports, an enquiry will be made from the Parliament Library whether they could find any use for them or could take them over for disposal under extant Instructional Orders, etc. The copies which the Library wishes to take over should be transferred to the Library; the others should be weeded out and disposed of according to the directions of the Branch Officer. 39 Other miscellaneous papers 5.41 The following miscellaneous papers will be weeded out after the lapse of the period mentioned against them:— (a) Parliamentary Bulletins and Circulars One year provided that at least 10 sets of each will be preserved for Future reference in addition to the sets maintained by Branches (b) List of MPs One year, provided that 10 copies of each list will be retained in the Distribution Branch for record (c) Beat lists of Parliamentary papers circulated to MPs Two years (d) Messenger Books (e) Attendance Register (f) Precedents Register (g) Used shorthand Note-Books with Stenographers/PAs Two years Three years As and when revised edition is brought out One year (h) Computer//Furniture Register [Estate Management Branch and Computer (HW & SW) Management Branches] Permanent 5.42 Regarding weeding out of records connected with accounts, the Branches concerned will observe the instructions contained in the Appendix XIII to Rule 289 of the General Financial Rules. However, some of the miscellaneous records relating to accounts will be weeded out as per the retention schedule given in Appendix XVII. 5.43 The weeding of all records will be supervised by the Head of Branch and the actual disposal done in his/ her presence. E-office based procedure for Recording and closing of files 5.44 In e-File the facility at recording a file is given for the files on which processing is done through physical and electronic file. An electronic file on which action is complete is closed and kept in a separate folder (closed folder). This may be closed by the creator of the file after getting approval of the competent authority, which may be of the level of Executive Officer or above based on the roles assigned in the application. The closed file may be seen by the official who has closed the file and official who has authorized the closure of the file. The closed title can be re-opened/retrieved by the official who has closed the file with the approval of the competent authority. The e-Files may be recorded under two categories:– Category ‘A’ — e-Files which qualify for permanent preservation for administrative purposes or historical reasons. Category ‘C’ — e-Files which are of secondary importance having reference value for a limited period. In exceptional cases, if the record is required to be retained beyond 10 years it will be upgraded to A Category. A soft/digital copy of such category of files (post closure) may be maintained separately in the Branch in the computer/ separate storage device. The said electronic files would be under the supervision of the Branch Head. The soft copy of the said files may also be forwarded to the Record Room as per the procedure outlined for Record Management. Weeding out of files in e-office The e-files once created in e-office are permanently retained. Such files after the scheduled period of retention may be closed with the approval of the competent authority. However, in case of physical file created through e-office the procedure as outlined above pertaining to weeding out of such physical file may be followed. 40 CHAPTER VI PRECEDENT REGISTER, ENTRIES FOR VARIOUS MANUALS AND MAINTENANCE OF RESEARCH MATERIAL 6.1 Not all decisions are taken by issue of orders or circulars. Often-internal decisions may be recorded on the notes portion for applicability within the Branches/Units concerned. Such decisions or precedents need to be properly identified and indexed for ready reference in future. For this purpose, a Precedent Register will be maintained in every Branch/Unit where decisions of this nature are taken (Appendix XVIII). This register may also be digitized and a soft copy should be maintained in a searchable format for easy reference for permanent record. A note of all important decisions and rulings made in the Branches /Units will be made in it. The Precedent Register is a guide to find out important decisions taken in the past in the Branches/Units, especially where the decision is not issued as a formal communication. A decision which is not recorded in the Precedent Register should not be quoted as a precedent. The Head of the Branch will mark the words “P.R.” on the file or receipt if the decision taken in it is to be incorporated in the Precedent Register. The register will be maintained by the Head of the Branch under his/her directions. The register is an absolute must in all advisory and regulatory Branches to ensure continuity and consistency of decision-making. 6.2 All entries in the Precedent Register will be classified under recognized headings and will be arranged alphabetically. The entries recorded in the register should be precise and clear and will be entered as shown in Appendix XIX. 6.3 An alphabetical table of contents, as shown in Appendix XX, will be prepared indicating main heading and sub-headings and page numbers allotted to them. Sufficient space will be left between each main heading and sub-heading for inserting other entries from time to time. 6.4 As soon as an entry under a new heading is made in the register, that heading will be shown in the table of contents at its proper place. 6.5 Entries under each heading will be started on a fresh page and entries under that heading will be entered one after the other with sufficient space between two entries. 6.6 As soon as a decision is taken in a file, it will be summarised and entered in the Precedent Register and shown to the Head of the Branch. The entries in the Precedent Register should also contain some background of the case or example wherever available. At the time of recording the file, a note will be recorded on the cover of the relevant file that it has been summarised and entered in the Precedent Register and the file will be submitted to the Branch Officer for information. 6.7 If a file does not contain any important decision, it will still be examined so as to find out whether it has any precedent value and the dealing hand concerned will submit the file to the Branch Officer with the suggestion whether or not it should be entered in the Precedent Register. 6.8 In every case where a file is not summarised but is entered in the Precedent Register, a note to that effect will be recorded in the relevant file. 6.9 At the end of each year the entries in the Precedent Register will be re-examined with a view to selecting those which contain important decisions or which have any precedent value. The entries selected for retention will be typed, given continuous serial number and submitted to the Divisional Officer (Director or Officer holding equivalent rank) for final approval. The entry in the Precedent Register relating to a decision, which becomes obsolete, should be deleted. 6.10 After the entries have been finally approved by the Divisional Officer (Director or Officer holding equivalent rank), the headings and sub-headings will be shown in the contents pages. These will then be printed with the following title in the Branch series. 41 Precedent Register of the Branch containing entries upto ….2022 (Vol I, II, III etc.) 6.11 At the end of every Lok Sabha, the various entries in the printed Precedent Register, will be further examined, integrated and reprinted in one volume. The following steps will be taken concurrently while summarising decisions taken on a file:— (a) Preparation of entries for Manual on Business and Procedure in Lok Sabha and Manual on Articles of the Constitution A suitable entry will be prepared for Manual on Business and Procedure in Lok Sabha and Manual on Articles of the Constitution, where necessary. Such entries will be prepared in the forms shown at Appendices XXI and XXII and will indicate in the margin the Rules/Articles, sub-rule/Clause etc. to which the entry pertains and the exact place where it should be inserted in the printed Manual. The entries will be submitted by the Branch concerned for Joint Secretary’s approval through their Branch/Divisional Officers. As soon as an entry is approved, two copies thereof will be made out by the Branch concerned, and forwarded to the Committee Branch-I. (b) Preparation of entries for Select Documents In the case of Branches dealing with Committee work, an entry will be prepared for inclusion in Select Documents after summarising and editing the important observations made by Chairperson, Secretary-General, Secretary or Members of the Committee on the functions, scope, procedure and the various other aspects of the Committee. These entries will be prepared on the model shown in Appendix XXIII and kept in folders for incorporation in the Select Documents of the Committee, to be printed from time to time. (c) Preparation of entries for Manual on Directions by the Speaker A suitable entry will be prepared for the “Manual on the Directions by the Speaker”, where necessary. Such entries will be prepared in the form shown at Appendix XXIV and will indicate in the margin, the Directions to which the entry pertains and the exact place where it should be inserted in the printed Manual. (d) Preparation of entries for Journal of Parliamentary Information Entries for short notes on important points concerning procedural matters of general interest and other parliamentary activities, such as Questions, Committee work, Privilege Issues, Conferences, etc., should be prepared, where necessary and sent to JPI Branch (LARRDIS) for incorporation in the Journal of Parliamentary Information. A model entry is given in Appendix XXV. (e) Preparation of entries for Departmental Decisions Entries will be made for incorporation in Departmental Decisions. Detailed instructions for the maintenance of Departmental Decisions are given in Chapter VII. 6.12 E-office based procedure for Precedent Entries In e-office, there is no provision for creation of e-precedent Register. NIC is the nodal agency for carrying out the necessary modification to incorporate e-precedent Register in the e-office application. As per the existing provisions available in e-office application, the following alternative method can be adopted as under: (i) In e-office application there is a provision of creating folders in the inbox. 42 (ii) As soon as the decision on e-file is taken, a new e-file comprising the summarised precedent entry e-file should be prepared. After the approval of the Branch officer, it should be placed in Summarised entry sub-folder under the main folder of precedent entry. The main e-file should be linked or attached to the precedent entry e-file for a reference to the main file. (iii) The e-files not containing the important decision may be placed in the Unsummarised sub folder also under the main folder of Precedent Entry, for examination or review, in order to decide the precedent value. (iv) The maintenance of precedent entry e-file in the digitized form would facilitate the review/ re-examination of the precedent entry content for retention/deletion at the end of each year culminating to the final publication of the Branch series. (v) Digitised precedent entry would also facilitate portability/transfer of approved precedent entries to the soft copy format of the precedent entry maintained separately in the prescribed format. Maintenance of research material, summaries of books, reference material, bibliographies, etc. prepared by Committee Branches and LARRDIS and supply of copies thereof to Parliament Library 6.13 As soon as the Branch concerned has prepared a research note or bibliography of permanent value, has summarised an important book, or has supplied useful material to a Member of Parliament in response to an enquiry received from him/her, one copy of each such work will be put up to the Divisional Officer (Director or Officer holding equivalent rank) who is administrative in charge of the Branch with a view to deciding whether the material should be placed in the Library for reference. Once decision is taken on the material to be sent to the Library, the same may be sent to the Research and Information (R&I) division of LARRDIS for uploading on Parliament Digital Library Home page. 6.14 All the Committee Branches shall give list of references such as Books, Reports of expert Committees/ Commissions appointed by the Government, Third party Evaluation Reports, Annual reports of Ministries, PSUs and Public Sector Banks (PSBs), Reports of regulatory authorities, etc. at the end of the report which shall also be uploaded onto the Lok Sabha Website. 43 CHAPTER VII COLLECTION AND PRINTING OF DEPARTMENTAL DECISION 7.1 All the i mportant decisions or orders by the Speaker on the various files will be collected by the Branches, as soon as those are taken and will be kept in the “Collection of Decisions” file, which will be maintained by each Branch. The decisions will be edited and made self-contained, so that the point for the decision is stated first, the background next, the views for and against the point and the conclusions of the competent authorities summarised thereafter. The summaries will contain the following:— (a) Main-heading at the top; (b) Sub-heading giving the gist of the Speaker’s decision (and not the general heading of the file); (c) Suitable catch-words of the sub-heading; (d) The number of the file from which the decision has been extracted. 7.2 Decisions given by Secretary-General/Secretary/Additional Secretary/Joint Secretary will also be incorporated in the collection. Printing of Departmental Decisions 7.3 At the end of every year these decisions will be printed in three different parts under the title “A selection from the (Departmental) Decisions Part.” The nature of the decisions to be included in each part and the Branch to be responsible for its compilation and printing will be as indicated hereunder: Nature of Decisions Branch responsible for compilation Part I Decisions regarding Parliamentary matters other than questions and Committees. Legislative Branch-I Part II Decisions regarding Questions. Question Branch Part III Decisions regarding Parliamentary Committees Committee Branch-I If, however, the number of decisions collected during the year is considered insufficient for the purpose of printing as a separate volume, these should be kept in manuscript and printed when sufficient material is gathered. 7.4 After the summary has been approved, copies thereof will be prepared in the form as shown in Appendix XXVI. 7.5 Two copies of each of those approved summaries will thereafter be passed on to the compiling Branch. The third copy of the summary will be retained as office copy in the Branch concerned for their record. 7.6 The compiling Branches will submit these decisions Branch-wise in batches of ten for approval of Secretary-General. After these have been approved by Secretary General, all the decisions will be consolidated by the compiling Branch concerned and arranged according to alphabetical order of the main headings and sub-headings, if any. 7.7 These decisions, when arranged, will be numbered serially. A table of contents and the index will also be prepared. 7.8 After the compilation has thus been finalised, a preface will be prepared and the compilation will be submitted for final approval. Thereafter, the compilation will be printed in the respective (compiling) Branch Series. 7.9 At the end of every five years, the compiling Branches will scrutinise the decisions included in their annual publications with a view to weeding out such decisions as might have become obsolete and print them in a single publication. 44 E-office based procedure for collection and printing of departmental decisions (i) In e-office all important decisions on various e-files would be available in the digitised format permanently. However, such files could be saved in the inbox folder of departmental decisions by the respective dealing hands of the Branch. (ii) Separate e-file with summarised departmental entry as per the prescribed format may be prepared by the dealing assistants in the e-office (with main e-file linked/attached to this file for reference). (iii) Post approval the same may be saved in another inbox folder summarised Departmental Decision entry. (iv) The soft copy of summarised Departmental Decisions may be forwarded to the compiling Branch, thus eliminating the need for maintaining physical copy of the above e-files. 45 CHAPTER VIII REVIEW OF PERFORMANCE, PUNCTUALITY , REGULATION OF ATTENDANCE AND OBSERV ANCE OF PROPER OFFICE DECORUM 8.1 To e nsure accountability and objectivity in the functioning of the Branches of the Secretariat, the following instructions have been laid down:— (a) Each Branch (other than a Committee Branch) will formulate an annual plan generally in the month of January while a Committee Branch will formulate its plan soon after selection of subjects for examination, wherever applicable. The plan will cover only important items of work. Routine matters will not be mentioned in the plan. The plan will reflect the manner and time-frame of action with month-wise break up of targets to be achieved in respect of each of the progammes and projects to be undertaken/subjects to be examined by the Branch during the ensuing year. The plan will also reflect available manpower in the Branch and its productive utilisation throughout the year. For House related Branches emphasis will be laid on programmes for inter- session periods. (b) The action plan will identify the levels of accountability, both direct and supervisory, for implementation of each action point. The plan will be discussed and finalised at the meeting to be held by the Joint Secretary (JS) concerned with the Branch and a copy of the approved plan sent to Secretary-General (SG). (c) Monthly performance report on the items of annual plan indicating details of targeted and actual performance and comments on variance, if any, will be submitted by each Branch to the JS concerned. The report should preferably be written by Heads of Branches and unnecessary embellishments should be avoided. Slippages in targets and problems, if any, in execution will be discussed and corrective measures be taken in the monthly review of performance by the JS concerned. (d) A quarterly appraisal report with reference to planned targets with comments of the JS concerned will be placed before SG for perusal. (e) As soon as monthly performance report/quarterly appraisal report is received back from JS/SG, the Head of the Branch will circulate it to the concerned Dealing Hand, etc. for taking necessary action in the light of observations made by the officers. (f) Model formats for quarterly/monthly review of performance of Committee Branches are given in the Appendices XXVII & XXVIII. Other Branches may, if considered necessary, modify the same or devise new formats to suit their special requirements. Office Hour 8.2 Except in Branches where shift system of duty or different duty hours are observed due to exigency of work, the normal office hours in Lok Sabha Secretariat are from 10.00 a.m. to 6.00 p.m. with half-an-hour lunch break from 1.00 p.m. to 1.30 p.m. In case of Staff Car Drivers etc. the normal reporting time for duty would be 9.30 a.m. to 6.30 p.m. or as detailed by the Branch concerned. Every member of the staff is expected to be in his/her seat during prescribed office hours. 10 minutes’ grace time may be allowed in respect of arrival time to cover any unforeseen contingencies. Such late coming (within the grace time) may be condoned unless it becomes a matter of frequent recurrence. Attendance and Punctuality To ensure punctuality and accountability of all the officers and staff of the Lok Sabha Secretariat, an Aadhar enabled Biometric Attendance System was introduced in the Lok Sabha Secretariat in 2018. [Ref: BAS, Circular Nos. 31174 dt 27th April 2018, 31354 dt. 17th Sep 2018, 31980 dt. 19.02.2020] In the instances of difficulties in registering the attendance through the said application, the employees(s) shall use physical attendance register available in the Branch for recording the attendance. [Circular No. 32676 dt.16th July 2021, 32267 dt. 29 Sep, 2020, 32413 dt. 11 Jan, 2021] Attendance Register 8.3 Every Branch including Reporters’ Branch and Interpreters’ Branch shall maintain an Attendance Register.
